MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "Jim Croce feels like a natural next choice because I want melodic songs and storytelling like the Simon & Garfunkel and Jonathan Edwards records I revisited.",
    "Olivia Newton-John, ABBA and Lesley Gore fit my interest in familiar pop songs collected in one place; Lesley Gore also connects closely with my mid-'60s listening."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The classical collection misses my current desire for songs with familiar voices; a relaxing mood alone does not make it appealing.",
    "The O Brother, Where Art Thou? soundtrack feels further from the melodic pop and folk hits I want today, while Bonnie Raitt and REO Speedwagon interest me without being my first choices.",
    "I cannot confidently choose the unnamed Greatest Hits album or Christmas collection without knowing the performers."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "A greatest-hits title seems to count too much on its own; the artist and the songs matter more to me than the collection format.",
    "My older rock and folk listening seems to have been stretched into a broader interest in roots music than my choices today support."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "Today I lean toward gentler melodic pop and folk storytelling, even though classic rock is also part of my listening.",
    "My latest Christmas album makes seasonal music relevant, but I still need a connection to the performers before choosing another collection.",
    "My interest in ABBA and Born This Way suggests that catchy pop can appeal across decades; nostalgia is only part of what draws me in."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations understood my interest in familiar pop collections, but sometimes treated compilation titles and broad musical connections as enough to explain what I want today."
}
